generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential or random unique integers within the observed range; never NULL; no duplicates.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Sample from the parent table's generated key pool; allow NULL with the compact share when the column is nullable; include at least one NULL row and at least one parent row without children.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_numeric: Uniform integer within the observed min/max; include boundary values at listed literals and one step on each side; NULL share per compact database when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_text: Random strings of length within the declared width; include near-variants (case, trailing space, one-character edit) of listed literals; NULL share per compact database when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_enum: Sample uniformly from the listed enum values; include near-variants of listed literals; NULL share per compact database when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_code: Random uppercase alphanumeric strings of the declared length; include near-variants of listed literals; NULL share per compact database when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.float_numeric: Uniform float within the observed min/max; include boundary values at listed literals and one step on each side; NULL share per compact database when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.distinct_columns: Ensure the duplicate share on DISTINCT columns is 20-50% by repeating values from a small pool.
generic_sampling_rules.order_tie_columns: Ensure at least two rows tie at the listed LIMIT rank on ORDER columns.
generic_sampling_rules.group_size_columns: Ensure group sizes of 1, 2 and >= 3 occur on GROUP columns.
generic_sampling_rules.aggregate_boundary_columns: Ensure counts straddle the listed HAVING literals (one below, one at, one above).
generic_sampling_rules.null_rule: Every nullable column gets at least one NULL row per instance; NULL share follows the compact database; planted NULLs are never replaced.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_probe_rule: Out-of-pool comparison-boundary literals (e.g. DNO 139/140/141/519/520/521) are query-side probes only; they are never stored in primary-key or foreign-key columns. Stored key/FK values always come from the parent key pool or are NULL.

uncertainty: Exact NULL shares per column are not given; use the compact database share and at least one NULL per nullable column.
Department.DNO boundary literals 140 and 520 are outside the observed DNO pool (10-90); they are query-side probes only and are never stored in PK/FK columns.
Minor_in.DNO boundary 140 is outside observed pool; query-side probe only.
Course.CID format is 'NNN.NNN'; near-variants preserve the dot and digit pattern.
Faculty.Rank tie direction is ASC per atomic summary; Department.DNO tie direction is DESC.
table_sizes_per_instance are exact per-instance generated row counts; jitter is not applied.
Group-size and aggregate-boundary shaping on key/FK columns must preserve uniqueness and referential integrity; verify post-conditions after dedup.

instance.py `_domain_sampler` looks up `spec.get('ranges', {})`, `spec.get('enums', {})`, `spec.get('codes', {})`, `spec.get('domains', {})`, `spec.get('boundary', {})`, `spec.get('cid_prefixes', ...)`. None of these keys exist in DEFAULT_SPEC (spec.py) nor in the supplied generation specification, which instead uses `semantic_rules_and_formulas` (e.g. `Age BETWEEN 16 AND 26`, `Credits BETWEEN 1 AND 4`, `Division IN ('AS','EN')`, `Rank IN (...)`, `Sex IN ('F','M')`, `Appt_Type IN (...)`, `gradepoint BETWEEN 0.0 AND 4.0`). Consequently the semantic domain rules are never applied by construction; columns fall back to generic samplers (NumberSampler/StringSampler) that can emit values outside the declared domains (e.g. Age outside 16-26, Credits outside 1-4, Rank/Sex/Division/Appt_Type outside their enums).
issues.requested_revision: Either (a) translate the specification's `semantic_rules_and_formulas` into the `ranges`/`enums`/`domains` structures that `_domain_sampler` consumes, or (b) extend `_domain_sampler`/`DEFAULT_SPEC` to parse and enforce the `semantic_rules_and_formulas` entries. Ensure Age∈[16,26], Credits∈[1,4], gradepoint∈[0,4], and Sex/Rank/Division/Appt_Type/Grade are drawn from their declared enums.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_apply_comparison_boundary` writes boundary probes (e.g. Department.DNO 139/140/141/519/520/521, Minor_in.DNO 139/140/141, Member_of.DNO 519/520/521) directly into the column values. For Department.DNO (a primary key) and for FK columns (Minor_in.DNO, Member_of.DNO), these probes are outside the parent key pool (observed DNO pool 10-90). Writing them into a PK column produces keys not present in the parent pool; writing them into FK columns produces dangling references. The spec's `uncertainty` explicitly notes these literals are outside the observed pool and should be 'boundary probes', not necessarily inserted as actual key/FK values. This conflicts with the FK integrity requirement and with `_fk_values` which otherwise draws only from the parent pool.
issues.requested_revision: Do not inject out-of-pool boundary literals into primary-key or foreign-key columns. Restrict comparison-boundary probes to non-key, non-FK columns, or route them through the literal pool used for query generation rather than into stored key values. Ensure FK columns only contain values from the parent key pool (or NULL).

issues.evidence: instance.py `_apply_unmatched_join` sets `out[0] = None` for columns listed in `unmatched_join_columns`, which includes `Department.DNO` and `Faculty.FacID` — both primary keys. Setting a PK to NULL violates the NOT NULL/PK constraint. Also `_apply_unmatched_join` is applied to non-FK columns (Department.DNO, Faculty.FacID) where the 'child rows with NULL FK' semantics do not apply.
issues.requested_revision: Apply the unmatched-join NULL planting only to nullable FK child columns (Minor_in.DNO, Member_of.DNO, Course.DNO, Course.Instructor), never to primary keys. Parent-side 'rows without children' should be achieved by leaving some parent keys unreferenced, not by nulling the parent key.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_apply_group_sizes` and `_apply_aggregate_boundary` rewrite values in place on columns including primary keys (Department.DNO, Course.CID) and FK columns (Minor_in.DNO, Enrolled_in.CID). Rewriting PK values after `_dedup_against_compact`/`sample_fresh_primary_keys` can reintroduce duplicates or collisions with compact rows (dedup runs before postprocess? — actually postprocess runs before dedup in build_random_instance, but the group-size rewrite can still create duplicate PKs that dedup then drops, silently shrinking the table and possibly breaking the intended group sizes). More importantly, rewriting FK columns (Minor_in.DNO, Enrolled_in.CID) to arbitrary values can produce dangling references.
issues.requested_revision: Apply group-size and aggregate-boundary shaping only to non-key, non-FK columns (e.g. Course.CName), or ensure any reshaping of key/FK columns preserves uniqueness and referential integrity (draw reshaped values from the parent pool). Verify post-conditions after dedup.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_fk_values` and `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` draw FK values from `_parent_pool(instance, ...)` which includes compact + generated parent values. However `_apply_comparison_boundary`/`_apply_unmatched_join`/`_apply_group_sizes` are applied to FK columns *after* `_fk_values` in `_postprocess`? — actually `_postprocess` is only called for non-FK columns in `build_random_instance` (FK columns are filled separately and not postprocessed). But `_apply_unmatched_join` lists FK columns and is only invoked via `_postprocess`, so it never runs on FK columns; the 'child rows with NULL FK' requirement is instead handled by `_fk_values` (first row NULL when null_share>0). This is acceptable, but the `unmatched_join_columns` list including PK columns (Department.DNO, Faculty.FacID) is misleading and, if ever routed through postprocess, would corrupt PKs. Also `_fk_values` forces `out[0]=None` only when `null_share>0`; for FK columns whose compact share is 0 (no NULLs observed), no NULL is planted, which may not satisfy 'at least one NULL row per nullable column'.
issues.requested_revision: Ensure every nullable FK column gets at least one NULL row per instance regardless of compact share (per the NULL rule), and remove PK columns from `unmatched_join_columns`. Confirm FK values are always drawn from the parent pool or NULL.

issues.evidence: writer.py `write_instance_sqlite` is called from cli.py as `write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p)` — without `orig_path`. In that branch the writer builds an empty clone from DDL and inserts *all* rows from `instance` (which already includes compact rows copied in `build_random_instance`). This means the compact rows are re-inserted from the in-memory copy rather than preserved from the original file. The docstring claims 'compact rows are never deleted or changed', but the actual path re-inserts them; if any compact row fails insertion (e.g. due to a constraint), it is silently dropped and counted as failed, violating preservation. Also `orig_path` is never passed, so the `shutil.copyfile` preservation branch is dead code.
issues.requested_revision: Pass `orig_path` to `write_instance_sqlite` from cli.py so the compact database is copied and only generated rows are appended, OR verify that the in-memory compact prefix is byte-identical and that insertion cannot fail. Ensure compact-row preservation is actually exercised and verified.

issues.evidence: instance.py `choose_table_sizes` uses `spec.get('table_sizes', {})` but DEFAULT_SPEC stores sizes under `table_sizes` (correct) — however the supplied generation specification uses `table_sizes_per_instance`. `load_spec` merges user spec over DEFAULT_SPEC; if specification.json uses `table_sizes_per_instance`, `choose_table_sizes` will not see it and fall back to DEFAULT_SPEC's `table_sizes` (which happens to match). This is fragile but currently consistent. More importantly, `choose_table_sizes` jitters sizes by ±25-33%, so the exact `table_sizes_per_instance` values are not honored; the spec says these are the per-instance sizes.
issues.requested_revision: Confirm whether exact table sizes are required; if so, remove or bound the jitter. Align the key name (`table_sizes` vs `table_sizes_per_instance`) between spec.py and the supplied specification.

issues.evidence: The specification's `semantic_rules_and_formulas` are stated as formulas (e.g. `Age BETWEEN 16 AND 26`) but the program's spec loader (spec.py DEFAULT_SPEC) does not encode them in a machine-consumable form (`ranges`/`enums`/`domains`). The specification also lists `comparison_boundary` values (139/140/141/519/520/521) that are outside the observed DNO pool and are described as 'boundary probes' — but it does not clarify whether these should be stored as actual key/FK values or only used as query literals. This ambiguity led to the PK/FK corruption issues above.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify in the specification: (a) provide the semantic domains in a structured form the generator can consume (ranges/enums per column), and (b) state explicitly that out-of-pool boundary literals are query-side probes, not stored key/FK values. Also clarify whether `table_sizes_per_instance` are exact or approximate.
